rationale_components.span: B's account is rich, additive, and tightly interlocking across all three rounds: the dry-room RH readings (31-34%, Quill at 32% at t=60) match round 1's per-panel values; the closing note by Mara Venn ('do not select a final panel yet, run two more cycles, reweigh Sedge, photograph the Quill corner split') coheres precisely with round 2's conclusion and both anomalies; tray numbering (Larkspur 1, Quill 2, Sedge 3) matches the one-tray-per-panel setup.

rationale_components.span: A, by contrast, shows the profile of a public-context bluff: a thin riff on exactly the four practices the shared context lists (trays, timed transfers, reference photographs, repeat observations), reactive denials of core content any such dossier would contain (room conditions/readings, panel construction, final entry), a recycled 'quirk' answer, and a self-contradiction on sample identification — round 1 asserted 'no individual panel names or inked identifiers are listed,' then rounds 2-3 quote a dossier line that 'each sample carries an inked identifier,' retrofitted with 'no identifier values are recorded.'
